title: Renewing Minds: Serving Church and Society Through Christian Higher Education, Revised and
description: "Be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may discern what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God." (Romans 12:2) Renewing Minds serves as a clear introduction to the field of higher Christian education, focusing on the distinctive, important role of Christian-influenced learning—both in the Kingdom of God and in the academic world. Union University president David S. Dockery writes for administrators, trustees, church leaders, faculty, and staff who are just beginning their service or association with a Christ-centered institution, and also to students and parents who are considering a Christian college or university. Chapters include: "Loving God with Our Minds," "Renewing Minds, Serving Church and Society," "Shaping a Christian Worldview," "Reclaiming the Christian Intellectual Tradition," "Integrating Faith and Learning," "Envisioning a Shared Community of Tradition, Belonging, and Renewing Minds," "Establishing a Grace-Filled Academic Community," "Developing a Theology for Christian Higher Education," and "Thinking Globally about the Future." New source information and footnotes have been added to this second edition. title: Higher Power: A Memoir of Brokenness, Redemption, and God's Grace: ONE MAN’S STORY OF OVER
description: When you hit rock bottom five floors underground in a foreign prison, there is nowhere left to look but up. Growing up in Sydney as the youngest child of hard-working Lebanese immigrants, Fred Nassif learned early how to survive and hide the struggles behind closed doors. A hidden family battle with gambling quietly shaped his youth, and by his early twenties, a single $5 win on a poker machine sparked a relentless addiction. That pull soon led him into illegal ventures, prison time, substance abuse, and the high-stakes world of Australia's outlaw motorcycle clubs and cage fight promotions. From the glitz of Gold Coast casinos to international business deals, Fred's search for fast money and loyalty eventually landed him in the middle of a devastating gold scam. Betrayed and trapped in an underground dungeon in Dubai, he faced the threat of a death sentence with no one left to trust. Stripped of everything and completely alone, Fred threw a blanket over his head and whispered a desperate prayer to the God he had long abandoned. What happened the next morning defied every odd, setting him on a path toward redemption, forgiveness, and peace, just in time to walk beside his beloved mother, Rita, through her final days. Raw, honest, and deeply moving, Higher Power is a true story of betrayal, survival, and the unshakable grace of God that proves no one is ever too far gone to be rescued.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0"]', '#CardInstanceggtF_KzpWDfjW6Ue4Vc_aQ')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_0',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:no

title: Spiritual Servants of the Most High God: 2026 Edition
description: Christianity has long embraced angelology, a theological study of angels. Unfortunately, this is a very simplistic view because the Bible actually speaks of a multitude of other spiritual beings, identified in this book as Spiritual Servants of the Most High. These spiritual beings may be discerned through discernment, which utilizes the five physical senses; touch, taste, hearing, sight and smell. Paul Cox and many others in Aslan’s Place operates in the gift of physical discernment and over the years God has taught them to discern the difference between good and evil as well as more than 200 aspects of God’s spiritual creation. But why is this important? Scripture is clear that Jesus only did what He saw the Father doing and that should be our goal as well. If we can discern what is happening around us spiritually, we can then come into agreement with the Lord regarding what He is doing. Spiritual Servants of the Most High God discusses just the first twenty-five beings that God taught Paul to discern. Prayerfully, this information will whet the reader’s appetite both for more discernment and increased understanding of the spiritual realms.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstancebyNMEQBtEKhMy_lCsFKQQw')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);height:20px;margin-right:4px;width:20px}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spi

title: BISHOP REEK ON THE CHRISTIAN LIFE: The Fire of God & the Salvation of Souls
description: There’s an empty chair at the lunch table. Everybody sees it. Who will pull it out and make room? Coach Joab Rico asks that question because of something Jesus did on the road through Jericho. He stopped, looked up into a tree, called Zacchaeus by name, and went home with the man the crowd would have passed by. In Bishop Reek on the Christian Life, a teacher and coach brings nine chapters of Scripture into the places his students know best. What does the cross mean to the kid who wears one around his neck? Where do you take your shame after a failure everybody saw? And when the last song at a revival ends, what does the Holy Spirit give you the courage to do on Monday morning? From “The Cross Is Not a Logo” to “Who Is Your One?”, Rico traces the Christian life from the grace that saves us to the joy of knowing Jesus and the courage to speak his name. The Seven-Day Heat Seeker Challenge gives students, coaches, and youth leaders a week of Scripture, honest questions, prayer, and practical steps. A five-page illustrated gospel tract closes the book. Saved by Grace. Satisfied in Christ. title: The Ant and the Sluggard: Slothfulness, Laziness and the Blessings of Diligeence (In Pursu
description: What if the greatest obstacle to your calling isn't a lack of ability, but the habits that keep you from moving forward? In The Ant and the Sluggard: Slothfulness, Laziness, and the Blessings of Diligence , Wilfredo Torres explores the timeless wisdom of Proverbs 6:6–11 and the powerful lessons God teaches through one of His smallest creatures. The ant demonstrates preparation, responsibility, and diligence without needing constant supervision. The sluggard, however, reveals how excuses, procrastination, fear, and neglect can quietly rob us of opportunities and spiritual growth. Through Scripture, practical examples, and the lives of biblical men and women such as Joseph, Ruth, Nehemiah, and Daniel, this book encourages readers to examine their habits, overcome destructive patterns, and develop a heart that honors God. Within these pages, you'll discover: How procrastination and neglect can affect your future Why diligence begins with the condition of the heart How to overcome excuses, fear, and the temptation to delay Biblical principles for becoming responsible and trustworthy How faithfulness in ordinary responsibilities prepares us for greater opportunities Why lasting rewards are connected to faithful living This book isn't simply about working harder. It's about developing the character, wisdom, and spiritual discipline to live faithfully in every area of life. Your next step toward a more diligent and purposeful life can begin today.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4"]', '#CardInstanceN3IG1QNLypv3BuOMVSyU3w')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary

description: My son was baptized in the name of God. My husband brought his mistress into the church where we promised to love each other forever. I thought the worst thing that could happen on my son's baptism day was crying in front of the congregation. I was wrong. For fourteen years, I loved Drew Calder. I built a home with him, raised our beautiful son, and believed the vows we made before God meant something. Then Camille Price walked into our church. My husband's mistress. Seven months of secret meetings. Seven months of stolen kisses. Seven months of coming home to me while giving himself to another woman. And he had the cruelty to bring her to our ten-year-old son's baptism. While our boy celebrated one of the most sacred moments of his life, his father was standing beside the woman who helped destroy our family. So I did the one thing nobody expected. I took off my wedding ring, placed it on the altar, and walked away. With my son. With my shattered heart. Without looking back. But leaving my husband was only the beginning. Our small town wants answers. Our church whispers about forgiveness. My son keeps asking questions that break my heart. And the literacy program I spent years building is suddenly threatened by a scandal I never created. Drew says he made the biggest mistake of his life. He says he still loves me. He says he'll do anything to bring us home. But where was that love when he was choosing her? I refuse to teach my son that love means accepting humiliation. I refuse to mistake an apology for repentance. And I refuse to let the man who broke my heart decide how quickly it should heal. title: One-Minute Short Devotions for High School Athletes: 100 Full-Season Devotions to Conquer
description: You love your sport. So why does game day feel so heavy? The tight stomach in the car. The replaying mistakes in your head at midnight. The fear of letting down your coach, your team, or the people in the stands. If that sounds familiar, you're not weak and you're not alone. Almost every athlete who cares about the game has felt it. This devotional was written for high school athletes who want faith that shows up in the locker room during their biggest games. Each entry takes about a minute to read and there will be one for every practice, benchings, bad calls, tough losses, and big wins. Inside, you'll find: 100 one-minute devotions that follow a full season, from tryouts and roster day through the regular season, playoffs, and off-season 100 verses with real sports applications , each paired with a game-day moment like a missed free throw, a hostile crowd, or a teammate who took your spot. A post-game reflection after every devotion , with quick fill-in prompts and simple Nerves and Joy ratings, so you can watch your nerves drop and your joy return over the season. The 10 traits of every successful athlete , each with a short Bible lesson and a practical drill. Pre-Game individual and team prayer guides , formatted for quick reading in the locker room, at halftime, after a loss, or in the huddle before the championship. Free bonus: A downloadable Game-Day Kit with printable locker-sized prayer cards, all 100 memory verses as cut-out cards, and a Nerves and Joy season tracker. Built for every sport and every scenario. title: Boston Loud
cats: Teen & Young Adult Coming of Age Fiction eBooks
description: Boston has never spoken a word. That doesn’t mean he has nothing to say. At eighteen, Boston is ready for the biggest year of his life. He has a best friend who can fill any silence, a family that has learned to hear him without words, a faith in God that belongs completely to him, and a new relationship with Rebekah that makes senior year feel full of possibility. But Boston also knows what it’s like to be seen for his disability before he’s seen as a person. Born with microcephaly, craniosynostosis, and cerebral palsy, Boston communicates through gestures, expressions, and an iPad while navigating a world that too often mistakes silence for emptiness. When unexpected seizures begin adding new uncertainty to his life, Boston finds himself facing questions no doctor, parent, or chart can easily answer. Still, life keeps moving. There are basketball games to play, buses to ride, jokes to make, a prom to look forward to, and people worth loving with everything he has. Told from Boston’s perspective, BOSTON LOUD is a funny, heartfelt novel about friendship, first love, family, faith, grief, and the complete person behind disability. It’s a story about being heard without speaking, finding purpose in a body that doesn’t always cooperate, and discovering that some of the loudest lives in the world are lived without a voice.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4"]', '#CardInstancevLOGt1Kn6tObMOE51NvwdQ')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_4',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color

title: Raising Godly Teens in a Smartphone World: A Christian Parent's Guide to Phones, Social Me
description: The childhood rules are not enough anymore. Your son or daughter is growing up in a world that fits in a pocket, and you want them to grow up in Christ. Raising Godly Teens in a Smartphone World is a calm, practical guide for Christian parents of adolescents. It sits beside Raising Godly Children in the Digital Age and goes deeper on the years when a device, a social app, and a hunger to belong all arrive at once. In this book you will learn how to: See your adolescent through Scripture, as a person being formed, not as a problem to manage Talk before you tighten the rules, so the relationship can bear the limits you set Build a family device plan that can actually hold, including when a phone is already in their hand Help them walk through social media, identity, and the fear of man without panic Speak honestly about purity, pornography, cruelty online, and new tools that write, talk back, or make almost-real images, with holiness and mercy Use technology for Scripture, friendship, service, and a living faith Send them out toward adulthood with your blessing still near The aim is not a perfect streak of screen-time. The aim is wisdom, stature, and favor with God and with people. This book offers step-by-step help, a copy-ready family agreement, and conversation starters you can use this week, with Scripture quoted from the King James Version and the World English Bible. You are not too late.
